##Load raw Data
Data from N = 157 heterosexual, naturally cycling women. Each row is the data from a single session.
See variable names below:

```{r raw data}
setwd("C:/Users/jjuenge/Desktop/data")
#rating raw data
data_raw <- read.csv("data_flirting_behavior.csv",sep =";",dec =",", header=TRUE)

#behavior measures
behaviors <- read.csv("behavior_measures_stimuli.csv",sep =";",dec =",", header=TRUE)

```

##Load cleaned combined long-format data
#Please check the OSF (https://osf.io/egjwv/) for description of variables and their names
 
#Data from n = 112 heterosexual, naturally cycling women who fit all inclusion criteria (positive LH tests, regular cycles, age...). Each row is the data from a single session.
 
```{r load data}
###load data frame with all women who had positive LH-tests and regular cycles (n = 112)
#this dataset is used for all main analyses!

setwd("C:/Users/jjuenge/Desktop/data")
data <-read.csv("data_behaviors_robust_cleaned.csv",sep =";",dec =",", header=TRUE)

##numbers as numeric, categories as factor variables
for(i in c(3,5,11:34)){
  data[,i] <- as.numeric(as.character(data[,i]))
}

for(i in c(1,2,4,6:10)){
  data[,i] <- as.factor(data[,i])
}

############################################################################################################
###load data frame including all women, used for robustness checks
setwd("C:/Users/jjuenge/Desktop/data")
data2 <-read.csv("data_behaviors_full_cleaned.csv",sep =";",dec =",", header=TRUE)


##numbers as numeric, categories as factor variables
for(i in c(3,5,11:34)){
  data2[,i] <- as.numeric(as.character(data2[,i]))
}

for(i in c(1,2,4,6:10)){
  data2[,i] <- as.factor(data2[,i])
}

###effect code relationship status
data$Relationship <- car::recode(data$Relationship, "'1' = '-1'; '2' = '1'")
data2$Relationship <- car::recode(data2$Relationship, "'1' = '-1'; '2' = '1'")

```

#This is how we subject-mean-centred the hormone values
```{r Subject-mean-centre hormones}


#add columns with log transformed hormone values for estradiol, progesterone and E/P, as reqested in the review process

data$log_Estradiol <- log10(data$Estradiol)
data$log_Progesterone <- log10(data$Progesterone)
data$log_E_P <- log10(data$E_P)

data2$log_Estradiol <- log10(data2$Estradiol)
data2$log_Progesterone <- log10(data2$Progesterone)
data2$log_E_P <- log10(data2$E_P)

#############################################################################################################
#add between-women values as requested in the review process

#for mean non-transformed, as well as for log transformed hormone values

data<-data%>% group_by(Person) %>% mutate(Estradiol_mean = mean(Estradiol, na.rm=TRUE), 
                                              Progesterone_mean = mean(Progesterone, na.rm=TRUE),
                                              E_P_mean = mean(E_P, na.rm=TRUE))

data<-data%>% group_by(Person) %>% mutate(log_Estradiol_mean = mean(log_Estradiol, na.rm=TRUE), 
                                              log_Progesterone_mean = mean(log_Progesterone, na.rm=TRUE),
                                              log_E_P_mean = mean(log_E_P, na.rm=TRUE))


data2<-data2%>% group_by(Person) %>% mutate(Estradiol_mean = mean(Estradiol, na.rm=TRUE), 
                                              Progesterone_mean = mean(Progesterone, na.rm=TRUE),
                                              E_P_mean = mean(E_P, na.rm=TRUE))

data2<-data2%>% group_by(Person) %>% mutate(log_Estradiol_mean = mean(log_Estradiol, na.rm=TRUE), 
                                              log_Progesterone_mean = mean(log_Progesterone, na.rm=TRUE),
                                              log_E_P_mean = mean(log_E_P, na.rm=TRUE))



#Scale untransformed mean hormones
data$Estradiol_mean <- scale(data$Estradiol_mean)
data$Progesterone_mean <- scale(data$Progesterone_mean)
data$E_P_mean <- scale(data$E_P_mean)

data2$Estradiol_mean <- scale(data2$Estradiol_mean)
data2$Progesterone_mean <- scale(data2$Progesterone_mean)
data2$E_P_mean <- scale(data2$E_P_mean)

#subject-mean-centre hormones
# and divide by a constant to put all hormones on ~ -0.5 to +0.5 scale
data <- data %>%
  group_by(Person) %>%
  mutate(Progesterone = (Progesterone - mean(Progesterone, na.rm=TRUE))/200,
         Estradiol = (Estradiol - mean(Estradiol, na.rm=TRUE))/10,
         Testosterone = (Testosterone - mean(Testosterone, na.rm=TRUE))/10,
         Cortisol = (Cortisol - mean(Cortisol, na.rm=TRUE))/7,
         E_P = (E_P-mean(E_P, na.rm=TRUE))/3) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  as.data.frame()
data %>%
  group_by(Person, Progesterone,Estradiol, Testosterone, Cortisol, E_P) %>%
  summarise(n = n()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  gather("hormone", "value", Progesterone:E_P) %>%
  ggplot(aes(value, colour=hormone)) +
  geom_density(alpha=.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-1,1))


############################################################################################################
###do the same for dataset including all women N=157
data2 <- data2 %>%
  group_by(Person) %>%
  mutate(Progesterone = (Progesterone - mean(Progesterone, na.rm=TRUE))/200,
         Estradiol = (Estradiol - mean(Estradiol, na.rm=TRUE))/10,
         Testosterone = (Testosterone - mean(Testosterone, na.rm=TRUE))/10,
         Cortisol = (Cortisol - mean(Cortisol, na.rm=TRUE))/7,
         E_P = (E_P-mean(E_P, na.rm=TRUE))/3) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  as.data.frame()
data2 %>%
  group_by(Person, Progesterone,Estradiol, Testosterone, Cortisol, E_P) %>%
  summarise(n = n()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  gather("hormone", "value", Progesterone:E_P) %>%
  ggplot(aes(value, colour=hormone)) +
  geom_density(alpha=.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-1,1))

################################################################################################################
######Exclusion of the outlier, participant number 187##########################################################

data <- data[- grep("187", data$Person),]
data2 <- data2[- grep("187", data2$Person),]

```

#Factor analysis for all behaviors and correlation matrix
```{r factor analysis}

measures <- behaviors[,c("v150atr","v150flm","v150sel", "M_gaze", "arrogance", "assertiveness","confrontative","dominance","fight","respected")]

#correlation matrix for Table S8
cor(measures)

#How many factors for exploratory factor analysis?
parallel <- fa.parallel(measures, fm = 'minres', fa = 'fa')

#test revealed 2 factors.
EFA <- fa(measures, nfactors = 2, fm="pa", rotate="oblimin", scores = "regression", use="complete.obs", max.iter=50)

#Show factor loadings (Table S9)
loadings(EFA)
print.psych(EFA, cut=0.3, sort=T)

#Save new factors, rename them and and merge to data and data2
behaviors2 <- cbind(behaviors$MaleID, EFA$scores)
behaviors2 <-as.data.frame(behaviors2)
colnames(behaviors2) <- c("MaleID","competitiveness", "courtship")
as.numeric(behaviors2$competitiveness)
as.numeric(behaviors2$courtship)

data <- merge(data, behaviors2)
data2 <- merge(data2, behaviors2)

cor.test(behaviors2$competitiveness, behaviors2$courtship)

#create new column with a new global factor (including the average value of both factors, as requested in the review process)
data$global_factor <- rowMeans(data[,c(44,45)])
data2$global_factor <- rowMeans(data2[,c(44,45)])


#do the factors predict sexual attractiveness and long-term attractiveness ratings?

sex_attr <- lmer(Rating ~ competitiveness + ( 1 | Person) + (1 | MaleID), data = data2)
summary(sex_attr)

sex_attr2 <- lmer(Rating ~ courtship + ( 1 | Person) + (1 | MaleID), data = data2)
summary(sex_attr2)

long_attr <- lmer(longterm_rating ~ competitiveness + ( 1 | Person) + (1 | MaleID), data = data2)
summary(long_attr)

long_attr2 <- lmer(longterm_rating ~ courtship + ( 1 | Person) + (1 | MaleID), data = data2)
summary(long_attr2)

```

#Robustness checks: controlling main analyses from the paper for inital testing session
```{r Robustness checks 1}
#Table S21
```
